items.title: No-stick restore writes the table before the EFI partition (power cut leaves no Windows, no way back)
items.fix_evidence: src/aurstage/rescue.c:1556-1604 the EFI partition is restored FIRST and only megabytes that differ are written (fault point restore-esp-mid at :1592); the table steps follow at :1605-1663 (restore-array :1622, restore-sector :1630, restore-backup :1663), then the NTFS grow. A cut before the table leaves AurOS in the table, so the saved copy is still findable and the restore can be run again. c994042.
items.test_evidence: tools/powercut-nostick.sh:287-350 (RESTORE_POINTS restore-esp-mid restore-array restore-sector restore-backup restore-grow; tear_esp makes two places in the ESP differ): at restore-esp-mid and restore-array 'AurOS is still in the table (6 partitions): it can be run again' (:325) and 'running it again finishes the job' (:328) plus full-size/byte-for-byte checks; at the later instants 'the EFI partition is byte-for-byte what it was (restored before the table)' (:341). items.proven_where: KVM/OVMF emulated disk, no-stick mode (the mode that ships). Never real hardware.
